title: Add comprehensive pytest‑flask tests for link creation and redirect endpoints
approach: Introduce a conftest fixture that clears the in‑memory store before each test to ensure isolation. Write new test modules covering the POST /links endpoint (happy path, missing/invalid payload, duplicate handling) and expand redirect tests for successful redirects, not‑found codes, and malformed codes. Use the pytest‑flask client fixture for HTTP calls and make assertions flexible for status codes and error messages.
tests_to_write: test_links.py::test_create_link_happy_path – POST /links with a valid URL returns 201 and a short_url field.
test_links.py::test_create_link_missing_url – POST /links with no url returns 400 with a detail indicating the field is required.
test_links.py::test_create_link_invalid_url – POST /links with an invalid URL returns 400 and an error mentioning invalid URL.
test_links.py::test_create_duplicate_link_returns_same_short – posting the same URL twice returns identical short_url values (idempotent).
test_redirect.py::test_redirect_happy_path – after creating a link, GET /<code> returns a redirect (301/302/307) with Location header matching the original URL.
test_redirect.py::test_redirect_not_found – GET on a non‑existent short code returns 404 with appropriate detail.
test_redirect.py::test_redirect_invalid_code_format – GET on a malformed short code returns either 400 or 404, asserting proper handling.
edge_cases: Missing required 'url' field in request payload.
Invalid URL format (e.g., not a proper scheme).
Duplicate URL submissions should yield the same short code.
Lookup of a short code that does not exist in the store.
Malformed short code strings (special characters, empty string).
Potential collisions in short code generation (handled by shortener logic).
